findings.description: CODE-SIDE SURPLUS (strongest). SHEET-TAB-001 lists 'Tax' as one flat tab among the four, each 'per-entity data band being one row per entity.' The real code (`render_tax` in sheets-view/src/lib.rs) actually splits Tax into TWO distinct typed ranges that must never merge: the accrual band (tab `Tax`, `TAX_HEADER` — 6 cols, one row per accrual) and a separately-named `Tax · Reserve Summary` range (`TAX_RESERVE_HEADER` — 7 cols, one row per (Jurisdiction, Tax Year)), enforced by `tax_accrual_band_has_no_among_data_summary_rows` and the embedded-header/blank-row assertions in tabs.rs. `TAX_RESERVE_TAB` is explicitly commented 'not a fifth entry in VIEW_TABS' but is still a distinctly-published range. All 3 B-runs reconstruct this split identically (B1 #7, B2, B3 #4). All 3 A-runs, working from the spec text alone, model Tax as a single flat `TabKind::Tax`/`TaxRow` band like the other three — none anticipate a second reserve-summary range, because nothing in SHEET-TAB-001 hints that one tab's 'entity' grain is actually two different grains.

SPEC-SIDE SURPLUS. SHEET-TAB-001 explicitly requires the four tabs be 'read-only.' None of the given code (sheets-view/src/lib.rs's `SheetsViewClient` trait, runtime/src/adapters.rs's `ViewSheetsAdapter`, runtime/src/sheets.rs's `SheetsApi`/`GoogleSheetsApi`) implements any protected-range, ACL, or permission-restriction mechanism — `GoogleSheetsApi`'s only `batchUpdate` calls are `addSheet`/`deleteSheet`; there is no `addProtectedRange` request or equivalent anywhere, and no trait method exposes a read-only/permission operation. All 3 A-runs, reading the spec text alone, treat 'read-only' as a real hard requirement and each explicitly punts it to an unmodeled external mechanism ('protected-range/publish pipeline,' 'enforced upstream,' 'outside this sketch') — i.e. every A-run had to invent a placeholder for behavior the spec text states, and nothing in the real code (as given) backs that placeholder up.

CODE-SIDE SURPLUS. `render_positions` enforces an explicit unwanted-behavior contract absent from SHEET-TAB-001: IF `Snapshot.positions` ever yields two entries for one symbol THEN it returns `Err(ViewError::DuplicateSymbolRow(symbol))` rather than emitting two rows — a defensive, structurally-unreachable-via-`Map` guard the design still requires 'error loudly if violated.' All 3 B-runs surface this near-verbatim (B1 #8, B2, B3 #5). No A-run's data model includes any duplicate-detection or error path — all three assume kernel-supplied entities are a priori unique with no runtime check, since nothing in the spec text raises the possibility.

CODE-SIDE SURPLUS. The republish write-discipline is a rich, tested contract nowhere in SHEET-TAB-001: row 1 (the frozen header) is written once and NEVER rewritten; only the data range from `DATA_START_ROW = 2` downward is rewritten as one atomic `update_range`, tail-truncated to the new row count — so a manually-inserted or sorted row is silently overwritten by design even when the new data is narrower/shorter (tabs.rs `republish_regenerates_data_and_never_rewrites_frozen_header`). All 3 B-runs converge on this exact mechanic and the exact constant `DATA_START_ROW`. The A-runs model only one-shot construction from kernel data (`publish_tabs`/`build_tab`/`publish_view_tabs`) with no notion of republish-over-time, truncation, or a frozen/never-rewritten header — that whole axis of behavior is invisible from the spec text alone.

CODE-SIDE SURPLUS. Each tab's header is a pinned literal schema — `POSITIONS_HEADER` (13 named columns), `OPEN_LOTS_HEADER` (10), `REALIZED_HEADER` (11), `TAX_HEADER` (6), `TAX_RESERVE_HEADER` (7) — with fixed column positions load-bearing elsewhere in the system: `adapters.rs`'s `price_reading_from_cells` hard-codes `PRICE_COL = 4` and `QUOTE_DATE_COL = 12` to parse the settle-pass read-back. SHEET-TAB-001 says only 'typed headers' — it names zero actual columns and asserts no positional contract. B2 and B3 both call out the exact column indices; B1 covers the same read-back/missing-tab contract without naming indices explicitly — still high agreement on the underlying point. No A-run invents any of these literal names or position pins (each fabricates its own generic header set, e.g. A1's `positions_headers()` uses only 4 columns: Symbol/Quantity/Cost Basis/Live Price).

CODE-SIDE SURPLUS. `workbook_tab_order()` fixes and idempotently reasserts on every republish a full 10-tab workbook order — the four view tabs, then `History`, then `Tax Rules`/`Residency`/`Platforms & Aliases`, then `Ledger Events`/`Tax Events` last — with Positions as the leftmost/landing tab (tabs.rs `workbook_order_views_then_config_then_logs_positions_landing`, `republish_idempotently_reasserts_tab_order`). SHEET-TAB-001 only enumerates the four view tab names; it asserts no tab-order requirement, no landing-tab semantics, and says nothing about tabs outside the four (History, config, event logs) at all. All 3 B-runs reconstruct this full order in matching detail; no A-run models anything beyond the four tabs it was asked to build.

RELATED GAP, both directions. SHEET-TAB-001's phrase 'typed headers' is underspecified, and each direction resolves it a different way that doesn't match the other. All 3 A-runs unanimously invent a declared per-column type enum (`ColumnType`/`CellType`: Text/Cents/Quantity/Percent/Date/Formula) meant to drive Sheets number/currency formatting. The real code has no such per-column type descriptor at all — `POSITIONS_HEADER` etc. are plain `&[&str]`, and the only 'typing' concept that actually exists is the binary `Cell::Value(String)` vs `Cell::Formula(String)` split (engine-written value vs. live GOOGLEFINANCE formula), which the code's own doc comment calls 'the whole point' of the Cell type — money/percent/date formatting is done as pre-formatted plain strings (`fmt_cents`, `fmt_shares`, `fmt_ppm`) before the value/formula split, not via a declared column type. All 3 B-runs, reconstructing purely from code, describe 'typed header' only as the literal frozen header text — none reconstruct a Text/Cents/Quantity/Percent/Date taxonomy, correctly reflecting that no such mechanism exists. So the spec's one ambiguous word pulls A toward inventing formatting-type metadata the code never had, while B confirms the code's real 'type' boundary is something else (value vs. formula) that SHEET-TAB-001 never mentions either.

notes: SHEET-TAB-001 is a single, highly compressed sentence relative to the actual sheets-view/runtime implementation. The A-direction (spec-only) surfaces one clean, unanimous spec-side gap: the code has no read-only/protection mechanism anywhere in the given files despite the spec mandating 'read-only.' The B-direction (code-only) surfaces a much longer, highly stable list of code-side invariants and constants (Tax's two-band split, the duplicate-row guard, frozen-header/atomic-truncate republish semantics, pinned literal header schemas with load-bearing column indices, and the full 10-tab workbook order) that SHEET-TAB-001 never states. Both directions were internally very consistent (high agreement) — A1/A2/A3 differ mainly in incidental implementation choices (e.g. A2 alone imposes an explicit row-sort by entity_id/symbol that A1/A3 leave to the kernel, and A2 alone restricts the GOOGLEFINANCE formula to Positions-only, which happens to match the real code) but agree on every structural point above. B1/B2/B3 are near-identical down to exact constant names (DATA_START_ROW, VIEW_TABS, TAX_RESERVE_HEADER, POSITIONS_HEADER), reflecting that they are transcribing the same literal source rather than interpreting anything ambiguous. Because both directions independently surfaced material, well-evidenced gaps against the same one-sentence requirement — even though the specific gaps differ in content — this is classified BD-DRIFT rather than a one-sided drift.
